title: Fairfax County Public Schools to Install XeedQ 4-Qubit Quantum Computer at Skyview High School - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Fairfax County Public Schools will install a XeedQ XQ1e 4-qubit room-temperature diamond NV-center quantum computer at Skyview High School in December 2026, billed as the first physical quantum hardware in a K-12 public school, coordinated via Connected DMV's Potomac Quantum Innovation Center as a regional talent pipeline.

insights.claim: XeedQ's XQ1e is a 4-qubit diamond nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center spin-qubit processor that runs at room temperature without cryogenic refrigeration, drawing about 500 W from a standard wall outlet.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Room-temp, plug-in systems open low-cost niches (education, edge) that cryogenic superconducting and many neutral-atom platforms cannot address.
insights.locator: The school district selected German deep-tech

insights.claim: The XQ1e reports single-qubit gate fidelities up to 99.9% and two-qubit gate fidelities up to 97%, with gate-level and pulse-level control via an open-source Python/Jupyter API.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: 97% two-qubit fidelity is well below leading platforms, positioning the device as a teaching/demo tool rather than a computational-advantage machine.
insights.locator: The school district selected German deep-tech

insights.claim: Leipzig-based XeedQ targets compact spin-qubit processors for mobile, educational and edge-computing use cases rather than large-scale fault-tolerant computing.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Signals a segmentation of the quantum hardware market where small-form-factor vendors compete on deployability, not qubit count.
insights.locator: Led by Founder and CEO Dr.

insights.claim: Fairfax County Public Schools, with Connected DMV and the Fairfax County Economic Development Authority, will install an on-premises quantum computer at Skyview High School in December 2026, reported as the world's first physical quantum hardware installation in a K-12 public high school.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Education is emerging as an early paying customer segment for low-end quantum hardware; watch for copycat district procurements.
insights.locator: Public school district Fairfax County Public

insights.claim: Student learning pathways built around the Skyview quantum computer are scheduled to launch in the Spring 2027 term.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Timeline to monitor for whether the deployment is real and replicable.
insights.locator: Public school district Fairfax County Public

insights.claim: The Skyview deployment is coordinated through Connected DMV's Potomac Quantum Innovation Center and is intended as a talent hub linking secondary schooling to universities, federal research labs and commercial defense-tech firms in the Greater Washington region.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Economic-development agencies are using quantum hardware to build defense-adjacent workforce clusters around DC, supporting local quantum/defense ecosystem formation.
insights.locator: Coordinated through Connected DMV's Potomac Quantum
